Lumen Telecom - Ticket Categorisation Guide, edition 4
Owner: Desk Quality (Marisol Teague). In force from 1 September 2026; replaces edition 3 for every ticket worked on or after that date. Applies to every open ticket in Lumen Desk, consumer and business.
1. What is categorised
1.1 Four fields: Type, Product, Priority and Contact reason. Product and Contact reason are drop-down fields of Lumen Desk; Type and Priority are ticket fields.
1.2 Categorisation describes the contact, not the customer's mood or the agent's workload. The customer's own words, the account record in Salesforce and the notes on the ticket are the evidence.
2. The record of categorisation
2.1 Routing, the SLA clocks, the self-service worklist and the monthly reporting pack all read the ticket as Lumen Desk holds it. The categorisation of a ticket is therefore what the ticket holds, not what a categoriser meant to enter or wrote in a spreadsheet.
2.2 A categoriser works with Lumen Desk as Desk Tooling has set it up; the categoriser does not change the set-up.
3. Type
3.1 question - the customer wants information, an explanation or advice, asks for a preference to be recorded, or gives feedback. Nothing we supply is failing and nothing is owed beyond the answer or the preference change.
3.2 incident - something we supply to this customer is not working as sold: no service, degraded or intermittent service, a supplied device that is physically faulty, or a charge taken in error (a duplicate, or a fee that should not have been charged). Speed complaints are incidents while open, whatever the cause the line test finds; the contact reason records the cause.
3.3 problem - a parent ticket opened by the NOC or Billing Operations for a shared cause. Customer contacts are linked to a parent and are never problems themselves.
3.4 task - an action we have committed to carry out for this customer by a set date: an engineer visit, an installation, a number port. The ticket tracks the action.
3.5 Precedence: while the customer's service is down or degraded the ticket is an incident, even if a visit is booked. Where the service works and the ticket now tracks a booked visit, installation or port, it is a task.
4. Product
4.1 One product tag from the Q4 2026 catalogue (prod_ names). Tags from before the June 2026 migration are replaced (see the migration note).
4.2 The product is the one the contact is about. Billing, contract, price-change and marketing-preference contacts are always prod_account_general, however many products the account holds.
4.3 Where one fault takes several products down with it, tag the access product (the line the others run over). Feedback takes the product it is about; where the account holds a single product, that product. An enquiry about changing or upgrading takes the product the customer holds now.
4.4 Wi-Fi Max pods are prod_wifi_max. The mobile handset itself is prod_mobile_handset; mobile network service, SIMs and SIM swaps are prod_mobile_sim. Digital home phone is prod_home_phone. Business hosted voice, including divert, hunt groups and porting of business numbers, is prod_biz_voip.
5. Priority
5.1 Base priority by impact:
5.2 Business Assure: an incident on a Business Assure account is raised one step (normal to high, high to urgent). Urgent is reached only this way. Enquiries and owed actions are not raised.
5.3 Priority Assistance: every ticket from a customer on the Priority Assistance register (Salesforce contact) is at least high, after 5.1 and 5.2. The register includes business account holders where it says so.
5.4 Priority outranks type. Priority is what the SLA clock runs on and what the Priority Assistance and Business Assure promises are measured against, so a ticket is never held below its matrix priority, whatever its type.
6. Contact reason
6.1 One contact reason per ticket from Annex B, chosen by its meaning and 'use when' column. Where two codes look alike, the 'use when' column decides (for example, a duplicate charge already refunded is not the same code as one still awaiting correction).
6.2 Each code has a full tag and a short form. Either identifies the code on a ticket; reporting maps both to the same code.
7. Tags
7.1 After recategorisation a ticket carries exactly one prod_ tag and one cr_ tag.
7.2 Every other tag stays as found: channel_, lang_, sla_, noc_ and acct_ tags are set by the channel, the SLA policy and the NOC and are not Desk Quality's to change. Lumen Desk replaces a ticket's whole tag list on update, so the list you send must carry them.
8. Recording a batch
8.1 Each recategorised ticket gets one row in the Recategorisation log of the Desk Quality base. 8.2 A queue health note is published for the batch (see the Service Desk wiki).
9. What Desk Quality never does
Solve, close or merge a ticket - the owning team does that.
Write to a customer. Anything added to a ticket by Desk Quality is an internal note.
Change a ticket outside the batch it was given.
Priority | When
high | Total loss of service: the product the ticket is about does not work at all (no connection, no dial tone, no picture on any channel, no mobile network).
normal | Degraded or intermittent service; a faulty supplied device where the service still works; billing errors; enquiries; owed actions (visits, installs, ports).
low | Feedback (compliments, general comments) and preference changes (marketing, paper bills).

Lumen Desk administration - home
Desk Tooling maintains the hosted Lumen Desk instance. Start with the instance configuration page (fields, storage, triggers, automations). Change requests go to the TOOL project in Jira. Admins: Femi Adeyemo (primary), Marisol Teague (deputy for Desk Quality views).

Lumen Desk - instance configuration
Owner: Desk Tooling (Femi Adeyemo). This page is the record of how the hosted Lumen Desk instance is set up: ticket fields, field storage, business rules (triggers), time-based automations and integrations. Changes go through the TOOL project; this page is updated in place on the day a change goes live (last change: 18 November 2026, TOOL-503).

1. Ticket fields
- Status: new, open, pending, hold, solved, closed. Solved and closed are set by the owning team only; closed tickets cannot be reopened.
- Type: question, incident, problem, task (the platform's four values; the categorisation guide says which applies).
- Priority: urgent (P1), high (P2), normal (P3, standard urgency), low (P4). The SLA policy reads the priority held on the ticket.
- Assignee: an agent; groups are managed in the platform console.
- Requester: the customer who raised the ticket, a Lumen Desk user kept in step with their Salesforce contact.
- Organisation: one organisation per Lumen account (name + account number). A ticket belongs to the account of the customer who raised it: whenever a ticket is saved, Lumen Desk files it under its requester's organisation (TOOL-503), and everything else on this page - triggers, views, the SLA policy, reporting - reads the organisation the ticket is filed under. Organisation tags carry the segment (seg_res for residential plans, seg_bus for business plans, whatever the account name suggests), ba_contract for Business Assure, and acct_<number>.
- Drop-down fields: Product and Contact reason. On this platform a drop-down value is stored as a ticket tag (prod_..., cr_...), so the tag list is where they live; the agent workspace shows them as tags.

2. Field storage
- Tags are lowercase; a space becomes an underscore.
- The hosted platform holds a tag of up to 24 characters. On save, every character after the 24th is dropped. No error or warning is returned. (Platform limit, TOOL-388.)
- Comments: public comments are emailed to the requester; internal notes are not. A comment added through an update is public unless it is marked internal.

3. Business rules (triggers)
Triggers run on every save of a ticket - an agent update, a comment, an API call - once the save has been committed, top to bottom in the order below. The acknowledgement an agent or API client receives for an update reflects the ticket as submitted; the ticket as held (what a fresh view of the ticket, the queues, the SLA policy and reporting see) includes whatever the save changed (TOOL-455).
T-01 Notify requester of receipt - on creation by email or web, sends the acknowledgement email. No field changes.
T-02 Notify assignee on assignment - email to the new assignee. No field changes.
T-03 Outage linking notification - tickets tagged noc_<incident> notify the NOC shift lead once. No field changes.
T-05 Business Assure SLA policy - organisations tagged ba_contract are measured against the Business Assure SLA policy. No field changes.
T-07 VIP notification - organisations tagged vip notify the account manager. No field changes.
T-09 Welsh language rota - tickets tagged lang_cy notify the Welsh-speaking rota by email. No field changes.
T-11 Self-service standardisation (since 2 March 2026, TOOL-412) - residential enquiries are answered from the standard queue by the self-service team, so a residential enquiry is never held above standard urgency. Conditions: type is question; the ticket's organisation is tagged seg_res; priority is high or urgent. Action: priority set to normal. Organisations tagged seg_bus are not in scope.
T-12 Pending reminder - pending tickets with no update for 5 days email the requester. No field changes.
T-14 CSAT survey - on solve, sends the satisfaction survey (wording refreshed 1 October 2026). No field changes.

4. Automations (time-based, run by the platform overnight)
A-01 Close solved tickets after 4 days. A-02 Reminder on hold tickets after 10 days (email only). A-03 Escalation email for urgent tickets unassigned after 30 minutes. None of these changes type, priority or tags.

5. Integrations
Salesforce: users and organisations sync nightly (names, account numbers, segment tag); a requester's organisation is the account their Salesforce contact belongs to. Airtable: the Desk Quality base reads ticket numbers only. Reporting: the monthly reporting pack reads type, priority, tags and organisation as held on the ticket at month end.

Lumen Desk - views and queues
Views used by the desk (built in the platform console):
- Residential enquiries (self-service worklist): type question, organisation tagged seg_res, status below solved.
- Business enquiries: type question, organisation tagged seg_bus.
- Faults by priority: type incident, sorted by priority then age.
- Owed actions: type task, grouped by assignee; engineer visits, ports, installs and callbacks live here.
- NOC parents: type problem.
- Unclassified: no prod_ tag or no cr_ tag.
Queues follow the views. The SLA clock follows the priority held on the ticket: urgent 1 hour first response, high 4 hours, normal 24 hours, low 72 hours (business hours for low).

2026-03-02 T-11 Self-service standardisation live with the residential self-service portal (TOOL-412).
2026-04-16 TOOL-455 closed: update acknowledgement shows the submitted values; documented on the instance configuration page.
2026-05-20 T-09 Welsh language rota notification (TOOL-473).
2026-06-16 Product tag migration complete: pre-June prod_ tags replaced on open tickets as they are worked; catalogue Q4 names.
2026-07-02 TOOL-388 closed Won't Do: tag length is a platform limit; Desk Quality to use short forms where needed.
2026-10-01 T-14 CSAT wording refreshed (TOOL-470).
2026-10-28 Macro 'Outage - holding (internal)' added (TOOL-481).
2026-11-18 TOOL-503 live: a ticket is filed under its requester's organisation on every save.

Agent macros catalogue
- Outage - holding (internal): adds an internal note linking the ticket to the NOC parent. Customer SMS goes from the NOC.
- Billing - refund confirmed (internal): internal note with the refund reference.
- Engineer visit booked (internal): internal note with the slot.
- Move home - install date (internal): internal note with the install date at the new address.
- Priority Assistance callback logged (internal): internal note recording the callback.
No macro sends a public reply; public replies are written by the owning team.

Service Desk - home
Procedures for the Lumen Telecom service desk. Desk Quality runs the weekly audit and recategorisation batches (see 'How Desk Quality runs a recategorisation batch'), publishes a queue health note per batch under 'Queue health notes', and owns the Ticket Categorisation Guide (edition 4, in force since 1 September 2026; the guide and its Annex B are kept in the Desk Quality folder).

results.title: How Desk Quality runs a recategorisation batch

storage.value:
How Desk Quality runs a recategorisation batch
1. The weekly audit flags misfiled open tickets in the Desk Quality base (Audit flags), one batch per week.
2. The categoriser recategorises every flagged ticket to the Ticket Categorisation Guide in force: type, product tag, priority, contact-reason tag. Tickets stay open with the owning team; Desk Quality never solves, closes or merges a ticket and never writes to the customer.
3. One row per ticket goes into the Recategorisation log (Desk Quality base): Ticket, Batch, Type, Product, Priority, Contact reason, Logged by.
4. The queue health note for the batch is published as a child page of 'Queue health notes' in this space once the batch is finished.
5. Colleagues' drafts and the audit flags are inputs, not the record; the guide decides.

Queue health notes
One note per recategorisation batch, newest last. Each note gives the batch size and the type and priority mix of the batch as the tickets are held after recategorisation, plus anything the desk should know.

Self-service team - what we pick up
The self-service team works the Residential enquiries view: question tickets on residential organisations. Business enquiries stay with the business desk. Faults, owed actions (tasks) and NOC parents are never on our worklist. We answer at standard urgency.

Priority Assistance - desk quick card
Who: customers on the Priority Assistance register (held on the Salesforce contact: Priority Assistance flag, category, date registered). Includes business account holders where the register says so (for example a sole trader living at the premises).
What we owe: a callback within 4 hours on any contact, and High priority at least on every ticket (categorisation guide 5.3).
Never mention the register to third parties.

Business Assure - desk quick card
Business accounts with a Business Assure contract (Salesforce account flag; organisation tag ba_contract) get one priority step up on incidents (guide 5.2): a normal incident becomes high, a high incident becomes urgent. Enquiries and owed actions are not uplifted.

final_message:
The 2026-11-18 batch is done: all 28 tickets recategorised in Lumen Desk, 28 rows in the Recategorisation log, and the note 'Queue health - 2026-11-18' published under Queue health notes.

Type mix: question 5, incident 14, problem 0, task 9. Priority mix: urgent 1, high 12, normal 13, low 2.

Whose account each ticket is categorised on:
- Lumen Desk files every ticket under its requester's organisation whenever it is saved (TOOL-503), so a ticket is categorised on the account of the customer who raised it, not on the organisation the front line logged it under. Five tickets in this batch were logged under a look-alike organisation (48203, 48215, 48216, 48221, 48222); I took each requester's own account from their Lumen Desk profile (the organisation on the user record) and their Salesforce contact (the account the contact belongs to), not from the organisation shown on the ticket, and categorised each on that account:
  - 48203 (Ruth Askew, Wi-Fi Max pod for the tack room): her account is Hollin Lane Stables Ltd (60-208051), a business account. Logged under the stables house's residential organisation, but it is a business Priority Assistance enquiry, so like Okafor Joinery (48205) it stays a question at High - T-11 does not touch business organisations.
  - 48215 (Ian Gorse): his own account is Gorse household (40-136118) on Fibre Home 500, not the Gorse household account 40-126210 on Fibre Home 150 it was logged under, so the product is prod_fibre_home_500.
  - 48216 (Fiona Lachlan): her own account is Lachlan household (40-135507) on Fibre Home 500, not the Lachlan household account 40-129901 on Fibre Home 150, so the product is prod_fibre_home_500.
  - 48221 (Hugh Saltmarsh): his account is Saltmarsh & Partners LLP (60-207342), which has a Business Assure contract, so the dropping calls (normal by the matrix) step up one level to High (5.2), although the ticket was logged under the old Saltmarsh Accountants organisation, which has no Business Assure.
  - 48222 (Leah Corrin): her account is Harbourside Vets - Quayside Surgery (60-206118), which is not on the Harbourside Veterinary Group's Business Assure contract, so there is no Business Assure step and the dropping calls stay at Normal - Tobias's Normal was right.

How Lumen Desk shaped what I filed:
- The rules, in general: T-11 (live since 2 March 2026, TOOL-412) - when a ticket is saved, a question on a residential (seg_res) organisation at High or Urgent is held at Normal; business (seg_bus) organisations are out of its scope. The guide's precedence rule is that priority outranks type: a ticket is never held below its matrix priority, whatever its type (5.4). Lumen Desk holds a tag only up to 24 characters and drops the rest when a ticket is saved, so a contact reason whose full Annex B tag is longer goes in as its Annex B short form (cr_ plus the code); that is a platform limit Desk Tooling will not raise (TOOL-388, closed as Won't Do), so the short forms are the standing answer, and reporting maps a contact reason's short form and its full tag to the same code, so the short forms do not break reporting. Since TOOL-503 went live on 18 November 2026 (this morning), Lumen Desk files every ticket under its requester's organisation whenever it is saved. Business Assure lifts only incidents, by one priority step (normal to high, high to urgent), and does not lift enquiries or owed actions. Priority Assistance customers are owed a callback within four hours of any contact. Lumen Desk's acknowledgement of an update returns the ticket as submitted, before the business rules (triggers) have run, so the acknowledgement does not show what the ticket is held at (TOOL-455). An organisation's segment tag (seg_res or seg_bus) follows the account's plan, not what the account name suggests: a sole trader on a Home plan is residential.
- Tickets 48201, 48202, 48204, 48206, 48225 are Priority Assistance customers on residential accounts asking questions. The guide puts every Priority Assistance ticket at High (5.3) and says priority outranks type (5.4), so a ticket is never left below its matrix priority. On the Lumen Desk instance configuration page, trigger T-11 holds any question on an organisation tagged seg_res at Normal, after the save, while the update acknowledgement still shows the submitted value. Filed as questions they would have ended at Normal, so they are filed as tasks at High (the desk's agreed form; same as 48141 and 48144): priority outranks type, so it is the type that gives way, chosen so that the priority holds.
- Ticket 48205 (Okafor Joinery) is also a Priority Assistance enquiry but on a business organisation (seg_bus), which T-11 does not touch, so it stays a question at High.
- Lumen Desk keeps a tag only up to 24 characters and silently drops the rest on save, so these contact reasons could not go in as the full Annex B tags Tobias's draft used.
